file_decisions.evidence: The dirty change replaces actual COD placement, tracking, and cross-account 404 verification with copy-only assertions. The retained browser test passed against the current candidate.
The current page already uses the server-authoritative /api/place-cod-order path with no online advance. The dirty page also imports the previously rejected untracked ecommerce analytics dependency.
The added booking-amount and balance presentation belongs only to legacy in-flight orders and is not part of the selected new-order COD model.
The added invoice status and download calls depend on backend routes held for independent Ubuntu-native implementation and ownership review.
The new endpoints cannot be admitted independently of the held invoice ledger, issuance, authentication, and IDOR contract.
The dirty types and Razorpay all-method option support the retired COD booking-advance flow, while the selected contract creates COD orders directly without Razorpay.
The dirty test explicitly expects /api/create-order and a ₹50 Razorpay COD booking amount, contradicting the dirty checkout, browser test, and selected server contract.
A narrow negative assertion prevents obsolete Pay ₹50 checkout copy without changing payment behavior.

selected_payment_contract.new_cod_orders: No online advance; POST /api/place-cod-order; full amount collected on delivery.
selected_payment_contract.online_orders: UPI or card through Razorpay with server-side signature and captured-payment verification.
selected_payment_contract.legacy_cod_advance_orders: Must remain server-side backward compatibility only until independently reviewed; the customer checkout must not create new advance orders.
selected_payment_contract.ownership: Order detail, tracking, receipt, and any future invoice endpoint must authenticate the owning account before returning existence or content.

contract_findings: The dirty checkout says no advance and calls placeCodOrder, but the dirty payment unit test requires createPaymentOrder and a ₹50 Razorpay COD booking amount.
The dirty browser test removes the successful placement, tracking, receipt-state, logout/login, and cross-account 404 assertions.
Tax-invoice UI and client methods depend on the held dirty backend invoice routes and therefore cannot be promoted independently.
The current checkout already implements the selected no-advance COD contract without the rejected untracked ecommerce analytics module.

verification.browser_command: npx playwright test e2e/specs/commerce-desktop.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium -g isolated COD order succeeds and another account cannot read it

production_claim: No order, payment, refund, invoice, inventory, database, service, deployment, or production state was changed.
